mainEntity.name: What factors drive the overall cost of building a mother-in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The overall investment depends heavily on whether your project is an interior renovation, a garage conversion, or ground-up new construction. Key cost drivers include running new plumbing branches and sewer lines for a bathroom, upgrading the electrical panel to support additional circuits, and adding heating and cooling systems. Interior conversions that use existing framing and subfloors generally require lower site preparation expenses than ground-up additions, which require excavation, concrete foundation slabs, framing, roofing, and full-house exterior finishes like stucco. Establishing specific layout priorities during the estimating process helps align the design with your target budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Overall costs are determined by the construction type—interior remodel versus ground-up addition—along with plumbing runs, electrical panel capacity, HVAC needs, and finished materials.
